newsitem.title: australia: Rugby union-Tombs dropped by New South Wales after ACT debacle.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Tombs dropped by New South Wales after ACT debacle.

text.p: New South Wales have dropped centre Richard Tombs and second rower Sam Domoni for the Super 12 match against Wellington on Friday.
New South Wales coach Matt Williams recalled veteran winger David Campese and forwards Phil Kearns and Fili Finau from injury for the vital clash in Napier.
Tombs and Domoni are the major casualties from the Waratahs' embarrassing 56-9 defeat against ACT Brumbies at Bruce Stadium on Saturday.
Domoni lost his place in a reshuffle of the forward pack, while Matt Dixon replaced Tombs in the backs.

The heavy defeat in Canberra all but ended New South Wales' hopes of qualifying for the Super 12 semifinals. They must win all three remaining matches to have any chance of sneaking into the top four in the standings.
Centre Graeme Bond and flyhalf Nathan Sponner were ruled out of the short tour to New Zealand because of injury.

Winger Chris Latham kept his place at the expense of Alistair Murdoch, who was named in the reserves, while Finau's return allowed captain Tim Gavin to move back into the second row from number eight.
Kearns, a former Australia captain and test hooker, start a match for the first time this season.

New South Wales - Matthew Burke, Chris Latham, Jason Madz, Matt Dixon, David Campese, Scott Bowen, Sam Payne, Fili Finau, Stu Pinkerton, Michael Brial, John Welborn, Tim Gavin (captain), Andrew Heath, Phil Kearns, Cameron Blades.
Reserves - Chris Whitaker, Christian Warner, Alistair Murdoch, Daniel Manu, Simon Kerr, Mark Bell.
